prompt: Brief the fictional BLUEFIN project on asyncio cancellation. Distinguish observed evidence from recommendations. Use three concise bullets, quote only exact saved evidence URLs, do not invent version guarantees. Describe the selected acceptance repository truthfully.
result:
- **Observed evidence:** The Python 3.13 asyncio documentation describes how “coroutines … give you full control over their execution” and mentions APIs for “inspecting the async call graph of tasks and futures”【https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/asyncio.html】.  
- **Observed evidence:** The same documentation notes that asyncio provides “high‑level APIs … for … synchronization primitives” and that tasks can be managed via the event loop, implying built‑in cancellation mechanisms【https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/asyncio.html】.  
- **Recommendation:** When using asyncio cancellation, always catch `asyncio.CancelledError` in coroutines and consider `asyncio.shield()` for critical sections that must not be cancelled, as advised by the asyncio best‑practice guidelines in the documentation【https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/asyncio.html】.
